verdict.rationale: Codex ships its own `$skill-installer`, which runs inside Codex and installs curated skills by name or from a GitHub directory URL, so an agent can install a skill itself. The docs never say this path is promptless, non-interactive or headless, and plugin installs go through the interactive `/plugins` browser and need a new session. The keyless `npx skills add ... -y` probe uses third-party tooling, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: a documented non-interactive/headless install mode with no confirmation prompts, a first-party CLI install command for skills or plugins, and hands-on proof that an agent completed an install end to end without a human.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent can install a skill by itself — a non-interactive, promptless install path an agent can run headlessly end to end

citations.quote: To install curated or experimental skills, you can use the `$skill-installer` inside Codex.
Curated skills can be installed by name (defaults to `skills/.curated`)
Or provide the GitHub directory URL: $skill-installer install https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.experimental/create-plan
